about: A Zork II-style underground cavern world. It starts in a barrow with a lantern and an Elvish sword, then moves through a tunnel, a ravine, a great cavern and a dark tunnel to a formal garden with a gazebo. The Wizard and the unicorn from the old games turn up as wandering presences.

done.why: I stopped early after about 12 turns, once I had seen the prose style and the opening rooms. I did not get into any puzzle. This is a short sample, not a full playthrough.

moments.note: The Wizard appeared when I turned on the lamp, and the narration gave him a wry line about peering as though I were not what he expected.
The lantern description says it looks like a thing that has been through one adventure and would rather not discuss it.
'examine copy of ZORK I' answered 'You can't see any such thing', although the room listed it.
A line about the room 'looking a little odd round the edges' settling down, with no explanation of what caused it.

wished: Examine the copy of ZORK I that the room listed.
Learn what the Wizard's spell actually did to the sword and the room.

lines.line: It has that look of a thing that has been through one adventure already and would rather not discuss it.
lines.why: Wry and self-aware. It sets the tone of the world as a sequel.

lines.line: He peers at you from under his bushy eyebrows, as though you were not at all what he had been expecting, and had turned up anyway.
lines.why: It adds character to a familiar figure.

lines.line: The walls are not the climbing kind.
lines.why: A compact way to say the ravine is a barrier.

fun.why: The opening is pleasant to walk through. I stopped before anything was at stake.

engagement.why: The tone is inviting, but I played too briefly to be pulled in.

difficulty.why: The first rooms are a straight path with no obstacles.

interestingness.why: It plays on Zork nostalgia with the Wizard, the unicorn and the room that goes odd. It also has the odd item that cannot be examined.

prose.why: The prose is dry and witty. The new lines are distinct from the classic room text, and the examine text is well turned.
